implementation_notes: Django provides the checkpoint directly: AuthenticationMiddleware populates request.user, LoginRequiredMiddleware (5.1+) makes every view require authentication by default with login_not_required() as the explicit public escape hatch, and login_required decorates single views; django.contrib.auth delegates verification to the configured AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS, the swappable mechanism. Flask uses before_request hooks or flask-login's @login_required, FastAPI uses dependencies and security utilities per router. These framework hooks replace the classic interceptor; hand-written middleware is justified only on a stack without one.
pitfalls: Middleware order matters: LoginRequiredMiddleware must run after AuthenticationMiddleware, otherwise request.user is the anonymous user for every request and everything is challenged.

request.user is a lazy object bound to the request; caching it at module scope or in a thread-local leaks identities between requests, and custom authentication backends must return None (not raise) for unsupported credentials.
